# LanQueue

> LanQueue (`lanq`) is a small .NET CLI that runs builds, tests and other allowlisted dev jobs on spare machines on your own LAN over SSH. It ships the current git state, picks the least-loaded capable machine, runs one command in a throw-away folder, streams the log, cleans up and returns the job's exit code. `--json` gives scripts and coding agents one result object on stdout.

The developer sets up the pool (`machines.yml`, allowlists, SSH keys); a coding agent only runs `lanq health --json`, `lanq run --json` (with `--dry-run` to preview; `--size`/`--min-size` and `--on` to route), `lanq run --plan --json --no-wake` (the jobs of the repository's `lanq.yml`; `--only`, `--dry-run`), `lanq doctor --json` (also `--remote`) and `lanq stats --json`, and follows the `nextSteps` lanq prints. It never edits `lanq.yml` or `machines.yml` to get around a refusal, and never runs lanq-makeready-fix (the script `lanq makeready` may point a PC's owner to): it is the owner's, run at that PC, local and interactive only.

Since 0.9.0 an agent may also add `--exclusive` (the job takes every slot of a machine; it waits for an idle one, with no reservation), `--baseline` / `--baseline-ref REF` (after a `Failed` run, the same command reruns at the base commit and the JSON gains `baseline.verdict`: `new`, `preexisting`, `inconclusive` or `skipped`; status and exit code never change) and `--env NAME=VALUE`, only for names the developer already lists in `machines.yml` `policy.allowed_env` and never with a secret (values are visible on the worker). It never edits `allowed_env` or `machines.yml` to get an `--env` through, reports a `preexisting` failure as such without trying to fix it unless that is its task, reports a `new` verdict with `sameMachine: false` with the caveat that it may be machine-specific, and reports the reason codes `env_conflict` and `windows_command_too_long` to the developer. An `ask_developer` step for an env refusal means stop and report, never drop variables or edit config to get through.

Since 0.9.2 the secret scan also reads the content of uncommitted files git shows as binary (a `.gitattributes` `-diff` or `binary` entry, UTF-16 text, real binaries), under caps; files over a cap are listed in `scanSkipped`. An agent never adds attributes, renames, compresses, moves or re-encodes a file to get past the scan, and reports `scanSkipped` and `scan-incomplete` refusals instead of fixing them. `lanq makeready` JSON is sanitised and filtered on every path, with `lanqWithheld` (lanq's own key) naming what was left out; `suggestedMachine` is advice for the developer and is never written into `machines.yml` by an agent. On Linux, the check that a `path_prepend` folder is safe also reads POSIX ACLs (as lanq-makeready 0.4.1); an agent never changes a worker's permissions or ACLs to get a folder proposed. In lanq's own repository an agent may run `lanq run --plan --json --no-wake`, never edits `lanq.yml` or its shard scripts to turn a red run green, and runs `scripts/smoke-workers.ps1` only when asked (it reads the developer's `machines.smoke.yml` from the per-user lanq config folder, `%APPDATA%\lanq\` on Windows or `~/.config/lanq/`; the repository's `machines.example.yml` is only a template that lanq never reads).

Since 0.10.0 `lanq run --plan` also takes `--on`, `--size` and `--min-size`, which narrow every job and never widen one (a job left with no machine ends the plan before anything is sent: `NoCapacity` 75, `retryable: false`, then `ask_developer` and a `fix_command` rerun whose `--only` lists the jobs that can still run); `--plan-timeout M` or `lanq.yml` `plan_timeout:` limits the whole plan (on expiry `TimedOut` 124 with `planTimedOut: true`, unless a `Failed` or `Rejected` job decides it); and `--fetch-dir`, `--fetch-max`, `--fetch-max-files` for every fetching job. `lanq.yml` `fetch_max` and `fetch_max_files` may only lower the 200 MB / 500-file limits and there is no `fetch_dir` key. An agent may narrow a plan and run the suggested rerun once (reporting the jobs left out), but never widens a job in `lanq.yml`, never raises `plan_timeout`, `--plan-timeout`, `--fetch-max` or `--fetch-max-files` to make a plan pass, and reports `fetchSkipped` instead. `lanq stats --json` adds `planJobs` (per plan file, by full path, and job).

`lanq doctor --json` prints one object with every setup check (`scope`, `machine`, `name`, `level` ok|warn|fail|skip|hold, `detail`, `fix`); `lanq stats --json` prints one object with the local job log's totals, per-machine times and speed factors, and per-command runs and `timing` (the work and per-shard overhead that `--shards auto --target-minutes M` uses to pick N).

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jangolath/lanqueue/main/README.md): what lanq does, install, commands, configuration and security model
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jangolath/lanqueue/main/AGENTS.md): short rules and decision tree for a coding agent that runs jobs through lanq
- [JSON output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jangolath/lanqueue/main/docs/JSON.md): every `--json` field, status and exit code (run, dry run, plan run, health, doctor, stats, makeready, init, wake), with jq and PowerShell examples
- [Agents guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jangolath/lanqueue/main/docs/AGENTS-GUIDE.md): setting up lanq for an AI coding agent, instruction-file snippets and a failure playbook

## Setup and use

- [Team quick start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jangolath/lanqueue/main/docs/TEAM-QUICKSTART.md): one orchestrator and a mixed pool of Windows and Linux workers, step by step (`lanq makeready --setup` and `--add`)
- [Workers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jangolath/lanqueue/main/docs/WORKERS.md): what each worker needs (OpenSSH, a build user, tools, Wake-on-LAN)
- [Plan files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jangolath/lanqueue/main/docs/PLANS.md): `lanq.yml` and `lanq run --plan`, several jobs (build, tests, a serial tail) routed by size across a mixed pool, one snapshot and one result; per-job `env:`, `exclusive:` and `baseline:`
- [Sharding](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jangolath/lanqueue/main/docs/SHARDING.md): splitting long test suites across the pool with `--shards`, picking N from history with `--target-minutes`, and balancing shards by duration, per ecosystem; the .NET recipe assigns each test class by a hash (`cksum`), the same on every machine and locale, with a guard script
